To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cDNA of the noncatalytical subunit of Rab 3 GAP, which is involved in the regulation of the exocytosis of neurotransmitter and hormone, was isolated and its primary structure and tissue distribution pattern was characterized.
we have cloned the noncatalitic subunit of Rab 3 GAP, a GTPase activating protein for the Rab3 subfamily of G proteins.
Rab3 GAP consists of a catalytic subunit, p130, and a noncatalytic, p150, and that p150 is essential for the localization of p130 in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular cloning and characterization of the noncatalytical subunit of the Rab GTPase activating protein.
the molecular cloning and characterization of the noncatalitic subunit of Rab GAP.
the cloning and characterization of the noncatalytically active subunit of a GAP for the Rab3 subfamily of the Ras-related small G proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p150 is a component of a Rab3 GAP complex, and that p130 is the catalytic subunit of this complex.
p150 is a noncatalytic regulatory subunit of the Rab GAP specific for the Rab subfamily implicated in the Ca2+-dependent regulated exocytosis.
the noncatalytically active p150 subunit is a subunit of Rab GTPase- activating protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Rab3 GAP is a heterodimer of p130 and p150 and that p130 is the catalytic subunit of the heterodimer.
Rab3 GAP consists of two subunits, one catalytic and the other noncatalytic, and both the subunits are necessary and sufficient for the GAP activity.
Rab3A GAP is a heterodimer composed of p150 and a p130-like protein and that the p150 subunit is essential for Rab3A GAP to be localized to the synaptic soluble fraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p150 is an integral part of Rab3 GAP.
the catalytic and noncatalytic activities of Rab3 GAP are not separable, and that the two subunits of Rab3 GAP may act together to regulate the Rab3 GTPase cycle.
the catalytic subunit of the Rab GTPase-activation protein (GAP), p130, is not sufficient to form the functional GAP.
